incident-bot: :rotating_light: INCIDENT (latency-slo): p99 token latency on streaming endpoints crossed SLO threshold in us-east-1. Auto-alerting oncall. metrics: https://grafana.redwood-inference/alerts/1867894320 :rotating_light:
Adele Chen: I'm paged, jumping in. initial ask: are we seeing spike on both hosted + dedicated?
Samir Patel: checking quick query -> dedicated fine, hosted streaming p95/p99 up ~2.5x, tail stalls look correlated with cache evictions.
Yang Li: seeing KV cache eviction rate climb starting +00:03, slab fragmentation high on streaming shards. Prefill hit-rate dropped, decode path still heavy.
Mike Novak: logs show a spike in prefill misses followed by synchronous decode fallbacks; a lot of small sequences causing frequent re-prefill -> eviction churn.
Jordan Reyes: customers impacted? any 5xx or only latency degradations?
Customer Success Bot: Notified CS team. Two customers have reported degraded streaming UX (latency >6s) in us-east-1, no 5xx so far. CS assigned: @Emily (not in thread yet).
Adele Chen: action plan: 1) short-term mitigation to reduce eviction churn, 2) triage root cause, 3) handoff for longer term. I'm going to try lowering prefill aggressiveness and bumping cache soft limits.
Samir Patel: +1. Where's the runbook for cache-pressure? runbook link: https://wiki.redwood-inference/runbooks/kv-cache-pressure
Adele Chen: following runbook commands now. running control-plane op to increase per-shard cache target by 20% and extend eviction grace window.
Adele Chen: command run (control plane):
```bash
# temp increase per-shard cache target
redwoodctl config set shard.kv_cache_target 1.2 --region us-east-1 --comment "incident 1867894320 temporary mitigation"
# extend eviction grace window to reduce immediate churn
redwoodctl config set shard.eviction_grace_seconds 45 --region us-east-1
```
perf-bot: Top traces for p99 (recent):
- stream-handler::prefill-miss -> sync-decode -> kv-evict (hot) -> stall (50-200ms) -> response
- heavy tail when sequence length variance > 512 tokens
perf-bot: heatmap: https://perf.redwood-inference/trace/1867894320
Yang Li: noticed decode threads are saturating GPU memory pinned buffers during sync decode fallbacks. Might be prefill vs decode imbalance: too many prefill attempts causing eviction, then decode blocks and stalls.
Mike Novak: rolled a small routing tweak: divert 10% of streaming traffic to a lower-memory model variant (compat-mode) to relieve decode pressure. Command: `routectl split-route streaming-us-east-1 --to fallback-compat --percent 10`
Adele Chen: customers dropped latency to ~1.4x within 90s after the config tweak and routing split. p95 trending down, p99 still noisy but improving.
Samir Patel: good. I'll start a deeper dump of KV allocation maps to analyze fragmentation; running collector now (may take few minutes).
Jordan Reyes: need to coordinate with Dedicated infra and Oncall SREs for longer term. Adele, do you want to handoff?
Adele Chen: Handing off active incident to Samir for post-mitigation triage and RCA. I'm going to update incident channel and notify CS.
Samir Patel: taking over. Current mitigations in place: increased cache target +20%, eviction grace 45s, 10% traffic routed to compat model. Immediate customer impact reduced. Next steps:
- complete KV slab/dump analysis (Yang)
- check allocator heuristics and prefill thresholds (Mike)
- evaluate promoting compat-mode if stable (Jordan)
- draft initial incident summary for CS and product
Yang Li: KV dumps collected -> uploading to infra bucket. early look shows heavy fragmentation on shards 7/9/12 caused by mix of short and long sequence workloads + small-alloc churn. Prefill code path allocates many small entries causing slab scatter.
Samir Patel: tentative root cause: workload mix + prefill strategy leads to frequent small-entry allocations -> slab fragmentation -> effective cache capacity drop -> increased eviction -> more prefill misses -> synchronous decode fallbacks -> tail latency spikes.
Adele Chen: CS notified: CS team posting proactive note to affected customers. Emily will follow up with customers that reported issues.
Mike Novak: quick mitigation proposal: 1) temporarily increase per-shard cache allocation (done), 2) bias prefill to compact small allocations into dedicated small-entry slab class, 3) reduce prefill attempts per request from 3 -> 1 for streaming until allocator changes land.
Samir Patel: agree. Rolling change for prefill attempts (canary 5%):
```bash
redwoodctl deploy-config streaming.prefill_attempts=1 --canary 5 --region us-east-1 --tag incident-1867894320
```
Jordan Reyes: I'll monitor logs for any regressions. If canary looks good, we can expand.
perf-bot: post-change metrics (2m after): p95 down 28%, p99 down 18%, streaming stall count down 35%.
Samir Patel: noting timeline for RCA. I'll open incident doc and assign owners. Draft will include mitigation timeline, affected customers, and recommended permanent fixes (allocator changes, prefill heuristics, slab compaction job).
Adele Chen: thanks team. I'll do a brief handoff note to oncall rotation channel and mark incident as "stabilizing". If any critical regressions, re-ping. :thumbsup:
Samir Patel: handoff ack. continuing triage.
incident-bot: INCIDENT UPDATE: status=stabilizing, severity=high -> assigned to Samir Patel. Link: https://incidents.redwood-inference/1867894320
_meta: generated by dataset-gen: realistic slack thread about KV cache fragmentation and live mitigation coordination
